A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ORACLE benchmark and black-box interaction framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 19 qualified LLM configurations, baseline screening, feedback comparisons, temperature and thinking ablations, and detailed per-environment results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds human evaluation, further controlled comparisons, reasoning-token measurements and black-box generation reliability results.

M1.justification: The exploration/evaluation procedure and three-module generation framework remain unchanged. Appendix G's generation and interaction prompts are substantively retained. Renaming black-box interaction and adding experimental prompt variants do not establish a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: The six tasks and 96 environments remain, but Appendix H.6 replaces Comparing Cards Ascending with Comparing Cards Slice, which uses a different opponent strategy. Appendix D.8 also adds evaluation of undergraduate and graduate participants on selected benchmark environments.

E2.justification: The screened model pool and 19 qualified LLM configurations are retained. v2 adds an actual human-versus-SOTA comparison in Table 10; v1 discussed human evaluation without reporting this comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds 5@1 and 30@2 evaluations, explicit prior-knowledge and reflective-instruction controls, and sampled human evaluation protocols. Several GSI environments change difficulty groups, shifting the benchmark from 50 easy/46 hard to 51 easy/45 hard. The original headline evaluation budgets remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained temperature, extended-thinking and delayed-feedback analyses, Appendix D adds studies of prior knowledge, exploration budgets, reasoning-token expenditure and reflective instructions, plus generation reliability and human evaluation. The extensive existing case studies are largely retained under Appendix F.

E5.justification: Both versions report three averaged runs for baseline screening. Neither adds empirical confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or seed information for the benchmark. Confidence parameters in v2's theoretical analysis do not constitute empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerous ablation and human results and replaces GSI scores. For example, o3's GSI 1@1 easy/hard averages change from 64.36%/41.43% to 79.43%/43.95% in v1 Table 5 versus v2 Table 11, under changed environment composition and grouping. The original detailed results for the other five tasks are unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix D's evaluation-correctness proof is removed. v2 Appendix C introduces a different theoretical framework: hypothesis classes, information and query-complexity bounds, task-specific identification arguments, and a formally defined exploration-efficiency ratio. This substantially changes the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: black-box interaction, the six-task ORACLE benchmark, automated environment generation, and the finding that LLMs struggle with efficient adaptive exploration. The headline model-ranking claims are also retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the new controls and human results, a speculative training-based explanation for planning failures, and a limitation concerning inaccessible model internals. It also adds real-world application mappings and an argument about generator neutrality, while removing v1's Goodhart's-law argument.

D1.justification: v2 documents difficulty assignment, human participant backgrounds and environment selection, and the exact reflective instruction. It fills placeholders in a GSI example. Existing API identifiers, principal budgets and prompts remain; the code link is retained, while website and leaderboard links are removed.

R1.justification: Appendix E.3 substantially expands positioning through comparisons with RULEARN, KORGym, PlanBench, TravelPlanner, Flex-TravelPlanner and work on chain-of-thought planning. It explicitly distinguishes exploration planning under unknown rules from plan execution under known rules. The Peirce discussion is relocated rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: The title and main-text terminology change to black-box environment interaction. Discussion and screening material move to appendices, Peirce background moves into the main text, and ablations and case studies are reorganized. New difficulty and impact sections accompany substantial restructuring.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Figures are resized and relocated, the baseline plot moves to the appendix, and six tables are added. Detailed result tables are redistributed, with revised GSI column groupings and extensive caption/layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added human comparisons, controls and research positioning provide useful evidence missing from v1. However, the new theoretical analysis asserts broad bounds without adequate derivations and introduces inconsistent summaries: Table 2 reports 64% for Xor Sequence at 10@1, while Table 15, retained from v1, peaks at 60% for that environment. These benefits and new analytical reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
